name: Fibromuscular Dysplasia of the Arteries of the Extremities

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography of affected arteries
Lack of atherosclerotic changes in affected arteries
Symptoms of limb ischemia such as claudication or coldness without other vascular disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic angiographic findings plus exclusion of other causes of arterial stenosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and exclusion of mimics such as atherosclerosis and vasculitis.

pathognomonic.notes: Pain induced by exertion due to arterial stenosis
Audible turbulent blood flow on auscultation

common.symptomName: Coldness or pallor of affected limb
common.notes: Due to reduced arterial blood flow
searchTerms: pale skin on affected arm or leg

common.symptomName: Reduced peripheral pulses distal to lesion
common.notes: Diminished or absent pulses on physical exam

searchTerms: fatigue in arm or leg with use

common.notes: Cooler skin temperature in affected extremity
searchTerms: one limb feels colder than other
skin temperature difference between arms or legs

occasional.notes: Pain at rest indicating more severe ischemia
searchTerms: constant aching in affected arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Numbness or paresthesia in affected limb
searchTerms: loss of feeling in arm or leg

occasional.notes: Swelling possibly related to venous congestion
searchTerms: swelling in affected arm or leg
muscle cramps in arm or leg

rare.symptomName: Ulceration or skin breakdown on affected limb
rare.notes: Due to chronic ischemia and poor wound healing
searchTerms: ulcers or wounds on arm or leg

rare.symptomName: Secondary hypertension due to renal artery involvement
rare.notes: If renal arteries are involved concomitantly
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery disease
secondary hypertension due to kidney vessels

imaging: CT angiography or MR angiography demonstrating multifocal arterial stenoses and aneurysms
Duplex ultrasonography showing turbulent flow and stenosis
genetic: No definitive genetic markers identified; familial cases rare
other: Physical exam findings of diminished pulses and bruits
Exclusion of other causes of peripheral artery disease

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors (smoking, diabetes, hyperlipidemia)
Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Histopathologic evidence of vessel wall inflammation

redFlags: Progressive rest pain or tissue loss
Signs of arterial dissection or aneurysm rupture
references: Olin JW, Gornik HL, Bacharach JM, et al. Fibromuscular Dysplasia: State of the Science and Critical Unanswered Questions: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2014;129(9):1048-1078.
